latest_nl_proof:
Fix n in N. First note that g(n) >= n: indeed, g(1),g(2),...,g(n) are n distinct positive integers in strictly increasing order, so the nth one must be at least n.

We prove the first displayed inequality. If g(n)=n, then g(g(n))=g(n), so
g(g(n)) - g(n) = 0 = (g(n)-n)(g(g(n)))^r,
and the claim is immediate.

Now assume g(n)>n. Then, by telescoping,
g(g(n)) - g(n) = sum_{k=n}^{g(n)-1} (g(k+1)-g(k)).
By the hypothesis of the lemma,
>= sum_{k=n}^{g(n)-1} (g(g(k)))^r.
For each k with n <= k <= g(n)-1, we have k >= n, hence (since g is strictly increasing) g(k) >= g(n). Applying the monotonicity of g once more gives
g(g(k)) >= g(g(n)).
Because r>0, the function x -> x^r is increasing on (0,infinity), so
(g(g(k)))^r >= (g(g(n)))^r
for every such k. There are exactly g(n)-n integers k in the interval [n, g(n)-1], therefore
sum_{k=n}^{g(n)-1} (g(g(k)))^r >= (g(n)-n)(g(g(n)))^r.
Combining the last three displays yields
g(g(n)) - g(n) >= (g(n)-n)(g(g(n)))^r,
which is the first claimed inequality.

For the second displayed inequality, note that g(g(n)) is a positive integer, so (g(g(n)))^r>0. Also g(n) >= 1, hence from the first inequality,
g(g(n)) = (g(g(n)) - g(n)) + g(n)
>= (g(n)-n)(g(g(n)))^r + g(n)
>= (g(n)-n)(g(g(n)))^r.
Dividing by the positive number (g(g(n)))^r gives
g(g(n))^{1-r} >= g(n)-n.
Thus both displayed conclusions hold for every n in N.

statement_nl:
Let r be a real number with r > 0. Suppose g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} is strictly increasing and satisfies g(n+1)-g(n) \ge (g(g(n)))^r for every n \in \mathbb{N}. Then for every n \in \mathbb{N}, one has
\[
g(g(n)) - g(n) \ge (g(n)-n)\,(g(g(n)))^r.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
g(g(n))^{1-r} \ge g(n)-n.
\]

domain_restrictions: r is a real number and r > 0
g is a function from the naturals N to N (codomain consists of natural numbers)
g is strictly increasing (so for all m>n, g(m) > g(n))
the hypothesis g(n+1)-g(n) >= (g(g(n)))^r is assumed for every n in N
exponentiation (g(g(n)))^r is taken with base in the image of g, which is a natural number (possible zero depending on convention for N)
the conclusion is asserted for every n in N
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all real r>0 and for every strictly increasing function g : N -> N satisfying (for all k in N) g(k+1)-g(k) >= (g(g(k)))^r, one has (for all n in N) g(g(n)) - g(n) >= (g(n)-n) * (g(g(n)))^r. Consequently (by adding g(n) >= 0 and dividing by (g(g(n)))^r when defined and positive) one obtains the weaker inequality g(g(n))^{1-r} >= g(n)-n.
quantifier_order: for all r in R with r > 0
for all functions g : N -> N that are strictly increasing and satisfy (for all k in N) g(k+1)-g(k) >= (g(g(k)))^r
for all n in N: claim holds

variables.name: n
variables.role: arbitrary natural-number argument (universally quantified in conclusion)

witness_dependencies: No existential witness is claimed; conclusions are universal in n.

To derive the displayed inequality for a fixed n one sums the assumed inequalities g(k+1)-g(k) >= (g(g(k)))^r over k = n, n+1, ..., g(n)-1. Thus the upper summation limit depends on g(n), which in turn depends on n.

For each summand with k >= n we use monotonicity: since k >= n, g(k) >= g(n), and because g is increasing, g(g(k)) >= g(g(n)). Hence each summand (g(g(k)))^r >= (g(g(n)))^r, producing a factor (g(n)-n).
